newsitem.title: USA: US EPA issues final rule on coastal oil, gas waste.
newsitem.headline: US EPA issues final rule on coastal oil, gas waste.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency issued a final rule Tuesday to stop oil and gas drilling waste discharges into coastal waters in the Gulf of Mexico and limit discharges into Alaska's Cook Inlet.
The rule, the final one under the Clean Water Act, is expected to reduce toxic wastes, such as arsenic and lead, going into the Gulf and Alaskan coastal waters by more than 200,000 pounds a year.
It should also reduce other pollution, including oil and grease, by 2.8 million pounds a year and waste such as ammonia and aluminum by about 1.5 billion pounds a year, EPA said.
State regulations already ban drilling waste discharges into the waters off California, Florida and Alabama.
Coastal waters are considered more sensitive to pollution than open offshore areas because the coasts have wetlands and complex ecosystems.
EPA said it would run more studies on fish tissues in Cook Inlet to evaluate the impact of pollution on people who depend on fishing in the area.
The final rule is expected to cost the oil and gas drilling industry $16.2 million.
